name: Giants of the Ice Age
description: Mammoths, sabre-tooths and ground sloths: the huge animals that early humans met and lived beside, and the great dying that took most of them.

checkpoints.name: Rise of the giants
checkpoints.note: As the climate cools, big animals such as ground sloths, glyptodons, sabre-tooths and giant apes spread over the continents.

checkpoints.name: A cold world
checkpoints.note: Glaciers advance and retreat. Woolly mammoths, rhinoceroses and cave bears roam the steppe while Neanderthals and then our own species hunt them.

checkpoints.name: The great dying
checkpoints.note: Modern humans reach Australia and the Americas, crossing Beringia, and within a few thousand years most of the world's largest land animals are gone. Painted caves such as Lascaux show the animals that people hunted.

checkpoints.name: After the ice
checkpoints.note: The ice retreats. A few giants such as the aurochs and the last mammoths linger, and the loss of species continues into modern times.
